items.title: The Wheel Number
items.question: Subjects spun a rigged wheel (10 or 65), then estimated African UN membership — medians landed near 25 versus 45. What moved the estimates?
items.correctExplanation: The random anchor — even openly random numbers drag estimates toward themselves. Adjustment from anchors stays insufficient, always.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the random anchor number. Expertise, news, and temperature miss it: Tversky and Kahneman's wheel proves irrelevance doesn't disarm anchors. Spin first, estimate second, drift inevitably.
items.lessonContent:
Irrelevance never disarms anchors.
Adjustment from starts stays insufficient.
Spin-then-estimate drifts inevitably.
Random numbers steer serious judgments.
Share this: anchor one estimate randomly.

items.title: The Listing Price
items.question: Real-estate agents appraising a house were swayed by its listing price — even while insisting they ignored it. What steered the experts?
items.correctExplanation: The listing-price anchor — Northcraft and Neale showed asking prices move appraisals while appraisers deny it. Expertise doesn't immunize.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the listing-price anchor. Data, charm, and coffee miss it: identical houses appraised differently by planted list prices. Denial accompanies influence reliably.
items.lessonContent:
Denial accompanies influence reliably.
Asking prices move appraisals silently.
Expertise never immunizes against anchors.
Identical houses price differently anchored.
Share this: ignore one listing price.

items.title: The Demanded Years
items.question: German judges given high versus low prosecutor demands (34 vs 12 months) sentenced the same shoplifting case very differently. What pulled the sentences?
items.correctExplanation: The prosecutor's anchor — Englich showed demands drag sentences even from experts explicitly warned. Justice weighs anchors, not just evidence.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the prosecutor's anchor demand. Remorse, temperature, and height miss it: dice-rolled demands moved judges measurably. Even random anchors sentence defendants.
items.lessonContent:
Demands drag sentences measurably always.
Justice weighs anchors alongside evidence.
Warnings fail against numeric gravity.
Even dice sentence defendants daily.
Share this: discount one opening demand.

items.title: The First Offer
items.question: In salary talks, whoever names a number first drags the final deal toward it — even absurd openings matter. What should negotiators do first?
choices: Let the other side anchor low
Set a high but defensible anchor
items.correctAnswer: Set a high but defensible anchor
items.correctExplanation: Set a high defensible anchor — first numbers frame every concession after. Absurdity backfires; ambition within reason pays.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is set a high but defensible anchor. Minimums surrender, passivity invites low anchors, acceptance forfeits negotiation. First numbers frame all that follows.
items.lessonContent:
First numbers frame all concessions.
Ambition within reason pays reliably.
Absurdity backfires; boldness banks.
Never accept opening frames passively.
Share this: anchor one negotiation high.

items.title: The Gandhi Ages
items.question: Asked whether Gandhi died before or after age 9 versus 140, then his actual age, subjects anchored wildly — medians 50 versus 67 (truth: 78). What explains the gap?
items.correctExplanation: The comparison anchor — even absurd bounds (9, 140) drag estimates: Strack and Mussweiler's selective-accessibility at work. Questions smuggle starting points.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the comparison anchor (9 vs 140). Education, data, and language miss it: the question's own numbers seed the answer. Asking frames answering, inevitably.
items.lessonContent:
Questions seed their own answers.
Absurd bounds drag estimates anyway.
Asking frames answering inevitably.
Starting points smuggle into verdicts.
Share this: spot one smuggled anchor.

items.title: The Phone Bid
items.question: Students asked whether they'd pay their phone-number-derived price for wine bid accordingly — digits became dollars. What leaked into valuations?
items.correctExplanation: Arbitrary digit anchors — Ariely showed social-security digits steering wine bids. Willingness-to-pay invents itself from noise.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is arbitrary digit anchors. Expertise, glass, and harvest miss it: meaningless numbers coherently move prices. Valuations construct themselves from available digits.
items.lessonContent:
Valuations construct from available digits.
Meaningless numbers move real money.
Coherent arbitrariness prices everything.
Digits become dollars too easily.
Share this: bid without one anchor.

items.title: The First Diagnosis
items.question: Doctors shown an initial (possibly wrong) diagnosis order fewer correct follow-up tests — thinking sticks to the first label. What traps clinicians?
items.correctExplanation: Diagnostic anchoring — Croskerry's error source: first impressions freeze differential diagnoses. Sticky labels cost lives quietly.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is diagnostic anchoring. Over-ordering, flattery, and noise miss it: minds dock at first diagnoses and adjust insufficiently. Reconsider deliberately, not by default.
items.lessonContent:
First labels freeze differentials badly.
Minds dock early and adjust thinly.
Sticky diagnoses cost lives quietly.
Reconsider deliberately, never by default.
Share this: rediagnose one settled case.

items.title: The River Length
items.question: Asked whether the Mississippi exceeds 500 versus 5000 miles, then its length, estimates split wildly around truth (~2340). What steered geography?
items.correctExplanation: The comparison anchor — Jacowitz and Kahneman: low versus high bounds drag confident geographers. Rivers run fixed lengths; estimates float on anchors.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the comparison anchor given. Projections, flows, and ads miss it: question-contained numbers steer answers reliably. Geography bows to arithmetic framing.
items.lessonContent:
Question numbers steer answers reliably.
Rivers fixed; estimates floating always.
Bounds drag confident experts too.
Framing governs geography quizzes.
Share this: estimate anchor-free once.

items.title: The Falling Fear
items.question: Travelers fear flying yet drive calmly, though per-mile driving kills far more. Dramatic crashes dominate memory. What inflates the flying fear?
items.correctExplanation: Vivid memorable crashes — availability: memorable deaths feel probable. Statistics whisper; footage screams.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is vivid, memorable crashes. Statistics, food, and seats miss it: ease of recall substitutes for frequency. Memorable is not probable, ever.
items.lessonContent:
Memorable never equals probable.
Footage screams; statistics whisper.
Recall ease substitutes for frequency.
Vividness inflates perceived risk.
Share this: fly one statistic calmly.

items.title: The Coconut Count
items.question: Falling coconuts kill ~150 yearly; sharks kill ~10 — yet beaches fear fins, not palms. What miscalibrates the dread?
items.correctExplanation: Availability of shark stories — films and headlines stock memory with fins. Palms kill quietly; screens scream sharks.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is availability of shark stories. Classes, ads, and shifts miss it: story supply, not death supply, sets fear. Fifteen-to-one reality loses to cinema.
items.lessonContent:
Story supply sets fear levels.
Screens scream; palms kill quietly.
Reality loses to cinema routinely.
Death counts need reading, not watching.
Share this: fear one palm proportionally.

items.title: The Ladder Odds
items.question: Terrorism dominates dread while ladders, bathtubs, and stairs kill thousands more yearly. What should recalibrate such fears?
items.correctExplanation: Base-rate statistics — annual death tables dwarf vivid threats into context. Denominators discipline dread.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is base-rate statistics. Movies, anchors, and headlines feed the bias: tables cure it. Ladders out-kill terrorists yearly — read the ledger.
items.lessonContent:
Ledgers cure vivid dreads reliably.
Denominators discipline all fears.
Tables dwarf headlines truthfully.
Base rates first, stories second.
Share this: read one death table.

items.title: The Visible Winner
items.question: Lottery advertising spotlights winners, never the millions funding them. What makes jackpots feel winnable?
items.correctExplanation: Availability of winner stories — advertised wins stock memory; silent losses leave no trace. Winnability is marketing's mirage.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is availability of winner stories. Machines, physics, and stores miss it: visible winners plus invisible millions equals false hope arithmetic. Funds never appear in ads.
items.lessonContent:
Visible wins hide invisible millions.
Hope arithmetic runs on ads alone.
Miracles marketed feel probable falsely.
Funders never grace billboards.
Share this: count one lottery's losers.

items.title: The Crash Seller
items.question: After market crashes, vivid losses drive investors to sell low — exactly when history favors holding. What sells at the bottom?
items.correctExplanation: Recency-fed panic — fresh crashes feel permanent; history's recoveries feel abstract. Selling low is availability monetized.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is recency-fed panic. Plans, dividends, and reports miss it: vivid red screens override century-long charts. Fresh pain discounts old recoveries fully.
items.lessonContent:
Fresh pain discounts old recoveries.
Red screens override century charts.
Recency monetizes investor panic.
Vivid present beats abstract past.
Share this: hold one crash calmly.

items.title: The Grieving Story
items.question: Grieving parents' vaccine-injury stories sway audiences more than million-child safety studies. What outweighs the statistics?
items.correctExplanation: Vivid anecdote availability — one televised tragedy outweighs a million-row table emotionally. Stories beat statistics in persuasion markets.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is vivid anecdote availability. Tables, salaries, and paint miss it: narrative transport defeats numerical literacy. Grief televised trumps safety tabulated.
items.lessonContent:
Narrative defeats numbers in persuasion.
Televised grief trumps tabulated safety.
Transport beats tables emotionally.
Anecdotes outweigh million-row studies.
Share this: table one anecdote tonight.

items.title: The Dangerous Block
items.question: Local news saturates violent crime while rates fall; residents feel danger rising. What inflates perceived risk?
items.correctExplanation: Heavy crime coverage — if-it-bleeds-leads programming stocks memory with mayhem. Perceived blocks grow dangerous on screen.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is heavy crime coverage. Census, budgets, and lights miss it: coverage volume sets fear volume. Falling rates feel rising when cameras multiply.
items.lessonContent:
Cameras multiply; fear follows footage.
Coverage volume sets fear volume.
Falling rates feel rising on screen.
Bleeds-leads stocks memory nightly.
Share this: check one real crime rate.

items.title: The Kayak Count
items.question: People insist more English words start with K than hold K third — though thirds dominate hugely. What misleads counters?
items.correctExplanation: First-letter recall ease — starters retrieve fluently, thirds resist: fluency poses as frequency. Tversky and Kahneman's classic K trap.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is first-letter recall ease. Fonts, songs, and keys miss it: retrieval fluency substitutes for counting. Easy recall feels like high frequency.
items.lessonContent:
Fluency poses as frequency reliably.
Retrieval ease substitutes for counting.
Starters retrieve; thirds resist.
Feelings of ease mislead counters.
Share this: count one letter honestly.

items.title: The Dramatic Germ
items.question: People rate botulism deadlier than asthma though asthma kills orders more yearly. Dramatic rarity beats common reality. What skews it?
items.correctExplanation: Memorable-case availability — Combs and Slovic: dramatic deaths inflate, mundane killers vanish from judgment. Rarity with narrative beats frequency without.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is memorable-case availability. Curricula, pages, and brands miss it: botulism's drama stocks memory; asthma's toll stocks morgues quietly. Narrative beats numbers in risk minds.
items.lessonContent:
Drama stocks memory; tolls stock morgues.
Narrative beats numbers in risk minds.
Rarity with story trumps frequency silent.
Mundane killers vanish from judgment.
Share this: fear one mundane killer.

items.title: The Saved Two Hundred
items.question: '200 of 600 saved' versus '400 of 600 will die' — the identical program draws opposite majorities. What flips the decisions?
items.correctExplanation: Gain-versus-loss framing — Tversky and Kahneman's Asian disease: saved-lives invite risk-aversion, lost-lives invite risk-seeking. Words move choices mathematics can't.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is gain-versus-loss framing. Math, diseases, and doctors miss it: identical outcomes choose differently described. Frames, not facts, decide under risk.
items.lessonContent:
Frames decide what facts cannot.
Saved invites caution; lost invites gambles.
Identical outcomes choose oppositely described.
Words move risk preferences reliably.
Share this: reframe one risk both ways.

items.title: The Surviving Ninety
items.question: '90% survive' versus '10% die' — the identical surgery wins different consent from patients and doctors alike. What moves them?
items.correctExplanation: Survive-versus-die framing — McNeil showed frames flip surgeons too: expertise doesn't exempt. Consent follows phrasing, not just prognosis.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is survive-versus-die framing. Tools, rankings, and coverage miss it: one mortality, two receptions. Even physicians choose by description.
items.lessonContent:
Description steers consent measurably.
Expertise never exempts from framing.
Prognosis identical, reception opposite.
Phrasing moves scalpels and signatures.
Share this: phrase one risk both ways.

items.title: The Penalty Nudge
items.question: 'Penalty for late filing' collects better than 'bonus for early filing' — identical money, different compliance. What works?
items.correctExplanation: Loss-framed penalties — losses loom larger than gains: penalties motivate where bonuses merely please. Framing moves money.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is loss-framed penalties. Budgets, forms, and deadlines miss it: same dollars, different psychology. Loss aversion is the taxman's silent partner.
items.lessonContent:
Losses loom larger than gains reliably.
Penalties motivate; bonuses merely please.
Same dollars, different psychology.
Aversion is the silent tax partner.
Share this: frame one incentive as loss.

items.title: The Lean Label
items.question: '75% lean' ground beef outsells identical '25% fat' beef. What sells the same meat better?
items.correctExplanation: Positive-attribute framing — Levin's beef: lean-frames taste better than fat-frames to buyers. Labels season perception.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is positive-attribute framing. Cows, grills, and packs miss it: identical meat, different adjectives, different sales. Framing seasons food before cooking.
items.lessonContent:
Adjectives season food before cooking.
Labels move identical meats differently.
Positive frames outsell negative twins.
Perception shops before mouths taste.
Share this: reframe one label positively.

items.title: The Pump Wording
items.question: Cash 'discounts' outperform card 'surcharges' for identical price gaps at gas stations. What frames the gap?
items.correctExplanation: Discount-versus-surcharge framing — gains delight, equivalent losses sting: wording prices the same cents differently. Thaler's classic pump.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is discount-versus-surcharge framing. Quality, colors, and smiles miss it: discount feels like gift, surcharge like theft — same gap. Wording moves wallets measurably.
items.lessonContent:
Gifts delight; thefts sting identically priced.
Wording moves wallets measurably.
Discounts feel; surcharges bite.
Same cents, different receptions.
Share this: discount, never surcharge, once.

items.title: The Default Organ
items.question: Opt-out countries harvest far more organs than opt-in ones despite identical public attitudes. What explains the chasm?
items.correctExplanation: Default-option design — Johnson and Goldstein: presumed consent keeps donors donors; opting out takes effort most skip. Inertia saves lives by default.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is default-option design. Surgeons, hospitals, and health miss it: attitudes match, defaults differ. Effortless generosity beats intended generosity massively.
items.lessonContent:
Inertia saves lives by default design.
Effortless beats intended massively.
Defaults decide what attitudes merely favor.
Presumed consent harvests compassion.
Share this: keep one good default.

items.title: The Automatic Saver
items.question: Auto-enrollment lifts retirement saving dramatically over opt-in plans among identical workforces. What does the default accomplish?
items.correctExplanation: Defaults harness inertia — Madrian and Shea: automatic saving sticks because switching takes effort. Laziness funds retirements.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is defaults harness inertia. Money, force, and markets miss it: enrollment by default converts procrastination into pensions. Design beats discipline for savings.
items.lessonContent:
Procrastination converts to pensions by design.
Laziness funds retirements automatically.
Design beats discipline for saving.
Inertia harnessed builds nest eggs.
Share this: automate one saving today.

items.title: The Warming Words
items.question: 'Global warming' versus 'climate change' shift concern and belief measurably across surveys. What moves opinions without new facts?
items.correctExplanation: Issue wording alone — Schuldt: warming triggers heat associations and skepticism triggers; change sounds milder. Labels move thermometers of opinion.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is issue wording alone. Thermometers, cores, and satellites miss it: same planet, different phrase, different concern. Wording is climate policy's quiet lever.
items.lessonContent:
Phrases move opinion thermometers.
Same planet, different concern levels.
Wording levers policy quietly always.
Labels precede beliefs in surveys.
